title: Moving Your Pieces
steps: Roll the dice by tapping the dice cup.
Tap a piece to select it — its legal destinations will highlight in green.
Tap a highlighted square to move your piece there.
If you have multiple pieces that can move, choose which one to move.
You must use the full roll value — if no piece can use it, the turn passes.
label: HIST3.1: In ancient Egypt, rosette was taught to children as a way to learn calculation and patience.

title: Capturing and Rosettes
steps: Move onto a square occupied by an opponent's piece to capture it — the captured piece returns to its start.
Rosette squares (marked with a rosette symbol) are safe — opponents cannot capture your piece there.
However, landing on a rosette with an unsafe piece (one that has been marked) ends the safety.
Capturing a piece earns you extra movement points — use them wisely!
label: HIST3.1: The rosette's protective power was believed to come from the goddess Sekhmet, who guarded the sacred squares.

title: Winning the Game
steps: Move all five of your pieces around the board and back to your home row.
The first player to get all pieces home wins the match.
If you win before your opponent moves any piece, it's a gammon — worth double.
In the circuit, winning at a tavern advances you to the next, harder tavern.
Collect omens from taverns to gain powerful abilities for future matches.
label: HIST3.1: Winning rosette was considered a sign of divine favor — the Egyptians believed the gods guided the dice of the skilled player.
